correctness.rationale: The absolute Fourier expansion gives one odd defect-bond Jacobi operator and one even rank-one diagonal-defect Jacobi operator. Their exact lower spectra yield both necessary-and-sufficient inequalities via density of discrete signed measures in weighted Fourier space. The strictness proof identifies the odd bound-state antipodal nulls and excludes realization of the even spectral null by finite atomic Fourier sequences using Cesàro uniqueness. The exact package checker passed 289 rational/quadratic-field assertions, including a negative eight-site quadratic form; these checks are corroboration, not a substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest prior explicit circular Poisson result determines the single sum-angle harmonic family with c=0 and therefore implies the c=0 slice but not the mixed c≠0 exact cone. The new contribution identifies an additional on-site Jacobi defect, a distinct negative-baseline phase, an exact strictness criterion and a boundary which is singular as an operator but strict on finite sets. The 2020–2022 nonisotropic harmonic frameworks give general criteria rather than this closed-form mixed family. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of absolute priority.

value.rationale: A natural three-parameter model combines stationary first-harmonic corrections with nonstationary sum-angle covariance in one Poisson smoothing family. The exact cone has two distinct spectral failure modes and a sharp phase switch at a=0; negative constant baselines may be rescued by stationary modulation, and even-boundary kernels remain strictly positive on every finite set. The explicit example where the odd bound permits b=4/5 but the true limit is sqrt(7)/4 shows that the even obstruction supplies essential additional information beyond a routine parameter scaling.
